prerequisites: Must have completed Year 8 (i.e. rising 9th grade or above; no upper grade restriction stated)
Sufficient English-language proficiency (English is the medium of instruction unless the specific project's faculty owner specifies otherwise)
program_dates: General window: 30 June – 15 August 2026 (High School track). Exact per-project dates vary by faculty mentor and are communicated directly to admitted students after acceptance, per the official page.
deadline: 15 May 2026 (2026-cycle window; official page displays this as part of a single 'Last Day to Apply: 23.03.2026 – 15.05.2026' line — see research_notes on interpretation)

duration: Not stated as a fixed duration for the High School track specifically. financial_aid: Explicitly free of charge ('Summer Research Programs are free of charge'). Accommodation/transportation is explicitly NOT provided for the 2026 Summer High School Programs (limited housing may be available for the undergraduate/graduate track only, per the official page).
selection_process: Students apply choosing from currently available KU faculty-led research projects matching their interest; accepted students are placed with a faculty mentor and that mentor's research group (which includes graduate/PhD students). The page has 'Required Documents' and 'Highschool Projects' accordion sections that could not be expanded during this research session due to a browser-automation tool instability (repeated timeouts) — their contents are left unknown rather than guessed.
individual_or_team: individual (placed into a lab/research group, not a self-formed team)
award_or_output: Participation certificate upon successful completion. No prize money, publication guarantee, or competitive ranking — this is a placement/mentorship programme, not a judged competition.
latest_verified_cycle: 2026 cycle — verified directly on the live official page (browser-rendered) on 2026-08-21; application window already closed, programme window (Jun-Aug 2026) concluding around the retrieval date.

research_notes: VERIFIED directly via a browser-rendered fetch of Koç University's own research.ku.edu.tr page (plain WebFetch was blocked with HTTP 403 on both research.ku.edu.tr and www.ku.edu.tr — likely bot detection; a real browser session succeeded): the programme genuinely places high-school students with individual faculty mentors and their research groups ('work closely with faculty mentors and their research groups that include graduate and PhD students') — this is the strongest genuine-mentored-research match found this session, and is explicitly, unambiguously open to international students, which is unusual among the Turkish leads investigated and worth flagging as high product value. VERIFIED: free of charge; Year-8-completion floor; no accommodation for the 2026 HS track. NOT VERIFIED / LEFT NULL: exact required application documents and the list of available high-school research project topics/fields for 2026 — both sit behind accordion UI elements ('Required Documents', 'Highschool Projects') that render collapsed in the page's static DOM; my browser-automation tool began timing out on scroll/click actions on this page before I could expand them, and I chose to honestly leave these fields null rather than guess or infer from the Undergraduate/Graduate track's content, which is described separately on the same page and is NOT confirmed to be identical for the High School track. AMBIGUITY flagged rather than resolved: the page's 'Last Day to Apply: 23.03.2026 – 15.05.2026' is a single line presenting what looks like a date RANGE under a singular-sounding label; I have interpreted this as application_open_date = 23 March and deadline = 15 May, which is the most natural reading, but the page does not itself use the words 'opens' or 'closes' to disambiguate, so this interpretation is noted rather than presented as certain. Similarly, a '7 weeks minimum' duration figure appears under a heading explicitly scoped to 'Graduate and Undergraduate Program Features' — I have NOT carried this over to the High School track's `duration` field since the page does not state it applies there too, even though it plausibly might; city was left null because, per this task's instruction to treat prior/training knowledge as an unverified lead rather than fact, I did not independently confirm Koç University's campus city on any page fetched this session.

subjects_fields: (25+ research tracks total per the official page; not exhaustively listed on the pages fetched)
delivery_mode: in_person (explicitly laboratory- and workshop-based: 'Laboratory experiments, mentored research projects, team-based project development')
prerequisites: Demonstrated interest in STEM (Science, Technology, Engineering, Mathematics) fields
Willingness to participate in laboratory and workshop activities
9th-11th grade prioritized; 12th-grade students may apply but are given lower priority
program_dates: Overall programme: 24 June – 27 July 2026; core laboratory/mentored-research internship period within that window: 29 June – 10 July 2026
duration: ~2 weeks of core laboratory/mentored-research work (29 Jun - 10 Jul 2026) inside a longer ~5-week overall programme window (24 Jun - 27 Jul 2026)
financial_aid: Explicitly free ('ücretsiz bir staj programıdır' — a free internship programme). No separate stipend or travel/accommodation coverage mentioned.
selection_process: Competitive; official page emphasizes passion for STEM, teamwork ability, analytical thinking and responsibility as selection criteria, matched against per-track quotas (cited on the page as ranging 1-15 students per track). 2026 cycle result, per İstinye's own news article: over 300 applications received, 110 students selected, drawn from many Turkish provinces and from both elite public science high schools (e.g. TÜBİTAK Fen Lisesi, Kabataş Erkek Lisesi) and well-known private schools (Robert Kolej, Koç Okulu, ENKA Okulları, Alman Lisesi).
individual_or_team: Students are placed into specific research tracks with per-track quotas (1-15 students cited); the official material emphasizes teamwork ability as a selection criterion and the news article describes 'team-based project development', suggesting small research teams per track, though the exact individual-vs-team structure per track is not fully spelled out on the pages fetched.
award_or_output: Certificate of participation for all who complete the programme ('katılım sertifikası verilecektir'); a closing 'Sunum ve Proje Sergisi' (Presentation and Project Exhibition) where standout projects receive additional, unspecified 'award and recognition support' ('ödül ve takdirle desteklenerek').
latest_verified_cycle: 2026 cycle — verified as complete via İstinye Üniversitesi's own news article (110 of 300+ applicants selected), dated approximately 2026-07-01.

research_notes: CLASSIFICATION DECISION: filed as `academic_program`, not `research`, because the official page's own framing describes fixed, structured coursework with lab exercises ('teorik bilgi sonrasında düzenli laboratuvar uygulamaları' — theoretical instruction FOLLOWED BY regular lab applications; 'paket program, ders seçimi yok' — a packaged programme with no course selection) rather than an independent, student-driven research project with a novel output. This is a deliberate contrast with this batch's other two records (Koç KUSRP, İstinye Genç Bilim İnsanları Akademisi), which both place students into individually mentored, open-ended research work — Sabancı's Nanotechnology summer school is real, well-run, and genuinely hands-on/lab-based, but its own materials describe it as guided instruction, not research. CONFLICTING EVIDENCE FOUND, recorded rather than silently resolved: the FAQ page states verbatim 'Son başvuru tarihi 1 Ağustos 2026'dır' (final application deadline is 1 August 2026), while the programme detail page pairs EACH of the three term dates with 'registration deadline May 1' (i.e. 1 May 2026) and separately states a cancellation-fee threshold keyed to 1 May 2026. These two official pages, both under sabanciuniv.edu, give two different deadline dates (1 May vs 1 August 2026) without any visible language reconciling them (e.g. 'early' vs 'final' deadline is not actually used on either page). Rather than guess which one governs, `deadline` is left null and this conflict is flagged here per this task's explicit instruction. VERIFIED: cost (79,500 TL, consistently stated on both pages), 2026 term dates, residential/Istanbul location, discount structure, certificate-only output (no research/competitive output). NOT VERIFIED / LEFT NULL: financial need-based aid (none found — only affiliation discounts); international-student eligibility; selection process nature (capacity-based vs. any academic screening was not made explicit).
